source.name: UNDRR Global Assessment Report 2025 Hazard Exploration: Droughts
source.publisher: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction

cadence: UNDRR GAR release review with annual drought-terminology and loss-estimate checks.
provenance: Official UNDRR global drought hazard assessment values. Recorded occurrence change, affected people, recorded economic cost and modeled present annual losses remain separate fields.
uncertainty: Drought onset, duration, direct and indirect losses and affected-population reporting are incomplete and definition-sensitive. The US$307 billion annual figure is an estimated current loss burden, not a reconciled observation inventory. The 1.5 billion affected count and US$125 billion recorded cost use the decade ending in 2017.
failure_behavior: Retain the last reviewed GAR assessment and mark stale; reject changed time windows or mixed loss-price boundaries. Never add affected populations across overlapping periods, turn a global occurrence trend into a local SPI value, or treat the modeled annual loss estimate as an observed ledger.

source_locators: GAR 2025 drought hazard exploration: at least 1.5 billion people affected and US$125 billion cost in the decade to 2017.
GAR 2025 drought hazard exploration: recorded droughts increased 29 percent over the past 20 years.
GAR 2025 drought hazard exploration: droughts are widespread and affect countries in every region of the world.
GAR 2025 drought hazard exploration: present drought-induced losses estimated at approximately US$307 billion annually (context only).

excluded_from_scoring: local SPI inferred from global impacts
